intro_html: This one eats like a rustic Italian dinner, with tender pork, white beans, tomatoes, and a little melted mozzarella on top. It is the protein champ of the group at 66 grams a bowl, all for about $3.20 a serving (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings from one pot is a hearty, filling week sorted.
cost_closing_html: About $3.20 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each serving delivers around 593 calories and a hefty 66 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Filling, comforting, and packed with protein. This is the bowl that keeps you full till dinner. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Canned cannellini beans are the base here, and they stretch the protein and fiber for about a dollar a can. No soaking required.
A little cheese goes a long way. One bag of reduced-fat mozzarella tops the whole batch, so buy the small size.
Canned diced tomatoes are always cheaper than fresh for a cooked dish. Keep a few cans in the pantry for meals like this.
make_it: Rub the pork loin with a little olive oil and set it in the slow cooker.
Add the diced tomatoes, chopped onion, and sliced red bell pepper.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork is tender.
Shred the pork and stir in the drained cannellini beans.
Cook another 15 to 20 minutes to warm the beans through.
Spoon into bowls, top with the shredded mozzarella, and let it melt before packing up.
